hyperedges.label: Card-to-merge branch lifecycle
Create Next App defaults superseded by project conventions
Transport run: fare snapshot, freight split, and signed receipt
Dated config resolution stack (one lookup, typed readers, never a default)
Audit trail integrity: blanket capture, append-only guard, revoked defaults
Append-only correction: reversal plus replacement
L1-only dated config setters sharing one preamble and BR23
Read views gating role in the WHERE while their tables stay deny-all
Go-live opening balance: a lot with no PO, a cost off the ledger, and a one-way close
Ledger immutability: three triggers closing UPDATE/DELETE, TRUNCATE and post-close OPENING
Traceability chain: supplier batch to dispatch round to lot to smoke-date group to ledger row
FINAL deny-all: the SECURITY DEFINER view is the only read door (no table policy ever lands)
Tables denied outright so an L3 session cannot reach a price or yield column (R20 / BR15)
Provisional deny-all: per-table declaration held until the card owning its role-specific v_* view is written
Tables held deny-all until their role-specific v_* view exists (ADR-002, ADR-004)
The L1 Owner single-read-door pattern: SECURITY DEFINER view gated on fn_current_role(), never a second table policy, and never force RLS
Tables whose closed posture is what keeps price and yield columns away from an L3 session (R20)
Tests that together prove the append-only stock ledger (ADR-003, R1)
Tests that together prove the deny-all RLS posture and the database-side role gate (ADR-004, R20)
Tests asserting the client-generated idempotency key survives a dropped connection (ADR-005, R4)

nodes.label: Next.js Agent Rules Block
nodes.rationale: This Next.js version has breaking changes from model training data, so agents must read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing framework code. The block is machine-generated and re-added by `next dev`, so deleting it from a diff only recreates an uncommitted change - committing it with the work keeps the tree clean.

nodes.label: node_modules/next/dist/docs (authoritative Next.js guides)
nodes.rationale: Resolved from AGENTS.md's own directory rather than the repo root, because in monorepos the `next` package may not be visible from the root.

nodes.label: Git Workflow
nodes.rationale: Documented in AGENTS.md rather than CLAUDE.md because CLAUDE.md is gitignored and AGENTS.md is checked in, so the workflow travels with the repo.

nodes.label: develop (integration branch)
nodes.rationale: Work starts from an up-to-date develop and finished work merges back into it with --no-ff, so each card stays visible as a merge commit. Card work is never committed directly to develop.

nodes.label: main (release-only branch)
nodes.rationale: Reserved for releases; direct commits are forbidden so the release line only ever moves through an integration merge.

nodes.label: feature/<short-slug> branch naming convention
nodes.rationale: English kebab-case named after the Tasks.md card, not after the files touched, so the branch name maps to board work rather than to implementation detail. fix/<slug> covers defects that are not cards.

nodes.label: One card = one branch = one merge
nodes.rationale: Keeps each unit of merged history traceable to exactly one board card. Branch first even for one-line changes; a second piece of work discovered mid-card becomes a new card on the board rather than an extra commit on the current branch.
nodes.norm_label: one card = one branch = one merge

nodes.label: Merge gate: acceptance line true, pnpm build and pnpm lint pass
nodes.rationale: A branch that does not build does not merge, so develop is always in a buildable state and the card's own Acceptance: line is the functional bar.
nodes.norm_label: merge gate: acceptance line true, pnpm build and pnpm lint pass

nodes.label: Create Next App scaffold README
nodes.rationale: Unmodified boilerplate from create-next-app: it still advertises npm/yarn/bun as interchangeable with pnpm, points at a root-level app/page.tsx, and describes Geist fonts - none of which match the project's actual pnpm-only, src/-nested, Noto Sans Thai setup.

nodes.label: next/font with Geist font family
nodes.rationale: next/font is used to automatically optimize and self-host the font rather than fetching it at runtime.

nodes.label: Deploy on Vercel
nodes.rationale: Recommended as the easiest path because Vercel is authored by the creators of Next.js and the platform tracks the framework's deployment model directly.

nodes.label: 000_revoke_defaults (schema-wide grant revocation sweep)
nodes.rationale: Defines no function. Exists purely for ordering: apply_state_folders() globs functions/ then views/ then policies/ alphabetically, so 000_ runs first and every per-file grant that follows is the last word. Undoes TWO default grants — Supabase's pg_default_acl named grant to anon/authenticated, and PostgreSQL's built-in EXECUTE to PUBLIC on every new function. alter default privileges covers only the first, for objects created later; it cannot pre-empt the built-in PUBLIC grant, which is why every function file still carries its own revoke line. Card ^ref-64; asserted by rls_deny_all_test.sql sweeps 1b, 1e, 1f, 1g against both Docker and live.

nodes.label: fn_add_po_delivery
nodes.rationale: Card ^ref-19 / D01: one dispatch round and its lot are one write, in one transaction, so a lot can never be orphaned from a round (lots.po_delivery_id is NOT NULL UNIQUE and there deliberately is no fn_create_lot). Enforces R4 idempotency (client-generated key; a replay returns the same lot id), BR03/R16/ADR-011 (foodiva_sent_weight_kg is frozen onto the lot as the yield divisor), BR11 (the lot must land at a CHEF_HOUSE location, never BRANCH or CENTRAL), and the PO over-delivery guard under `select ... for update` on purchase_orders so two concurrent 60 kg rounds cannot both commit against a 100 kg PO. Boundary is `>` not `>=` — cumulative exactly equal to ordered is a fully delivered PO. seq is derived under the lock, never a parameter, because round order drives v_po_outstanding and every FIFO view. Touches no stock_ledger row: a booked round is a plan, not a movement.

nodes.label: fn_allocate_freight
nodes.rationale: Card ^ref-23 / R24, ADR-012, BR16, D04.1: splits a transport run's fare across its lines and asserts in the database that the rounded shares sum back to run_cost_thb to the satang, raising FREIGHT_RECONCILE_FAILED otherwise. The remainder lands deterministically on the largest line by dispatched weight, ties broken on smallest id, so a re-run never moves a satang between lots. Reads alloc_method off the run row (snapshotted at creation, R29) and never from config at call time, so a later config change cannot move a closed number (BR23). Zero fare means two different things: on CENTRAL_TO_BRANCH it is correct and returns quietly (R25); on any other route it raises RUN_FARE_NOT_SET. MANUAL refuses rather than silently producing a weight split wearing a MANUAL label. The idempotency key is taken but not stored — the function inserts nothing and re-running is deliberately supported; it is the only writer of freight_share_thb.

nodes.label: fn_audit_row (generic audit trigger function)
nodes.rationale: Card ^ref-06 / R32: ONE trigger function for every table, so the audit shape cannot drift between tables and a table added by a later card cannot silently skip the audit. SECURITY DEFINER is correctness, not hardening — audit_log is deny-all with zero grants, so the insert must run as the owner (force row level security must never be turned on there). Reads actor and role straight from profiles rather than fn_current_role(), because that helper folds in is_active and goes null for a deactivated caller, and a deactivated session that somehow writes must still be logged. Branches on tg_op rather than CASE because referencing OLD in an INSERT trigger raises. row_id is RESOLVED, not assumed (^ref-62): `id` when it casts, otherwise the table's single-column uuid primary key, otherwise null — opening_costs (PK ledger_id) logged a null row_id and opening_balance_close (PK id boolean) made `'true'::uuid` take down the very insert it was auditing. business_date wins over event_date per ADR-007, and the reason column is coalesced across the schema's three spellings.

nodes.label: fn_audit_log_append_only
nodes.rationale: TC-18: an audit trail that can be edited proves nothing. Unconditionally raises AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY so audit_log is insert-only and only the audit trigger inserts. Needs two trigger attachments because Postgres fires neither UPDATE/DELETE nor TRUNCATE events for the other — a before update-or-delete trigger alone would leave TRUNCATE free to empty the log.

nodes.label: trg_audit_log_append_only (before update or delete on audit_log)
nodes.norm_label: trg_audit_log_append_only (before update or delete on audit_log)

nodes.label: trg_audit_<table> attach loop (blanket audit trigger over pg_tables)
nodes.rationale: DO block that creates or replaces an after insert/update/delete row trigger calling fn_audit_row() on every table in public except audit_log itself (which would recurse). Because this is a state file re-applied on every deploy, a table created by a later card is covered without anyone remembering to come back here — the failure mode migration 0005's RLS loop had.
nodes.norm_label: trg_audit_<table> attach loop (blanket audit trigger over pg_tables)

nodes.label: fn_backdating_allowed
nodes.rationale: Card ^ref-62 T4: R28's back-dating window as ONE function rather than a flag read at eight future call sites, so fn_record_sales, fn_record_waste, fn_record_thaw and fn_close_daily_report cannot each re-derive `current_date - k` and disagree about inclusivity. ADR-021's relaxation is the whole first branch: while opening_balance_close is empty, every back-dated ordinary row is accepted, and the rule re-arms by consequence when fn_close_opening_balances writes its row — no second mechanism. The boundary is INCLUSIVE of its last day (settled by the Owner 9 Sep 2026); 0 means today only. Uses current_date, not now()::date, because the window is measured in Asia/Bangkok business days (ADR-010, ADR-014) and a UTC-evaluated boundary silently gives or takes a day at a 01:00 cutover. CONFIG_NOT_SET propagates — an unset window is a named refusal, never an assumed 3. Granted to authenticated because it reveals only a boolean about a date, so a screen can grey out a date picker (ADR-004).

nodes.label: fn_check_variance
nodes.rationale: ADR-019 / R22: the single variance rule — round(abs(actual - expected) / expected * 100, 2) — called by branch Diff (R23), central intake (R27), transport receipt (BR12) and physical counts (R19), so the tolerance cannot come to mean three different things on three screens. Refuses three things: dividing by a zero or null expectation (returns NULL pct and REASON_REQUIRED, never a reassuring 0%); guessing ALERT vs BLOCK (p_mode has NO default, so an omission is a compile-time miss); and rounding after comparing (20.004 rounds to 20.00 and is inside the band, so the number on screen and the verdict beside it agree). Threshold is a parameter defaulting to R22's 20.00, not a literal buried in the body (ADR-006, ADR-018). The file's old `drop function if exists` had to be removed at ^ref-22: v_transport_variance is now a hard catalogue dependency, the drop failed on the second apply, and because 000_revoke_defaults runs first the aborted file left the function executable by nobody.

nodes.label: fn_close_opening_balances
nodes.rationale: Card ^ref-62 T7 / ADR-021: closes opening balances one-way, permanently, for everyone. The completeness check and the close are deliberately the SAME operation (TDD Seam 1) — split apart, a row entered between check and close leaves a costless lot in an append-only ledger for ever with no path to fix it. The idempotency key is load-bearing rather than ceremonial: the same key returns the committed closed_at (R4 retry), a different key raises OPENING_ALREADY_CLOSED (TC-29); catching unique_violation and re-raising unconditionally would turn every dropped connection into a permanent-looking refusal on an operation the Owner cannot retry or undo. Completeness is a LEFT JOIN from stock_ledger OPENING rows to opening_costs, because the cost lives in a second table (the ledger refuses UPDATE), and the refusal names both the count and the lot codes so the Owner can act on it. R28 re-arms by consequence via fn_backdating_allowed, not by a second statement. Audit row comes from ^ref-06's generic trigger in the same transaction, never written here.

nodes.label: fn_config_boolean
nodes.rationale: Card ^ref-22: the boolean arm of ^ref-11's config resolution. config_settings has value_numeric/value_text/value_json and no value_boolean column, so partial_receipt_allowed and receipt_variance_requires_reason need a cast ladder that accepts `true`, `"true"` and 1 depending on which screen wrote the row — written per call site across F5, F8, F9 and F11 that is a dozen places to get wrong. Numeric 1/0 is accepted; any other number raises CONFIG_WRONG_TYPE rather than guessing which way a magic number means true. CONFIG_NOT_SET propagates from fn_config_value and is never defaulted to false: a missing flag read as false is a rule silently switched off, and worse than a false rate because a false flag looks like a decision (ADR-006, BR23). EXECUTE granted to NOBODY — config_settings holds prices and R20 keeps L3 out of them, so only SECURITY DEFINER fn_* callers can reach it.

nodes.label: fn_config_date
nodes.rationale: Card ^ref-62: the third typed reader over fn_config_value, existing because config_settings has no date column and ADR-021's go-live opening_cutoff_date has nowhere to live but text. The cast lives here rather than inside fn_record_opening_balance so that ^ref-61's readiness view cannot re-derive it and disagree about what a malformed value means — one function, one place it can rot. A malformed date is CONFIG_WRONG_TYPE, never a null and never a caught-and-defaulted today() (ADR-023, BR23). value_numeric always raises: 20261001 and an epoch day count are both plausible and mean different years, and guessing is how a cut-off silently moves. EXECUTE granted to nobody, same posture as its two siblings; named in sweep 1f of rls_deny_all_test.sql.

nodes.label: fn_config_value
nodes.rationale: Card ^ref-11 / R12, ADR-006, ADR-018: one dated lookup for thirty config keys, returning the whole config_settings row so text and jsonb keys use the same resolution as numeric ones and adding a key stays a data change. CONFIG_NOT_SET is a RAISE, not a null — a null invites coalesce(..., 0) at a call site and a zero rate produces a settled-looking figure, the exact failure ADR-006/BR23/BR04 exist to prevent. p_event_date has no default, because now() would resolve a closed period against today's rate. SCOPE BEATS RECENCY: a branch-scoped row wins over a global row even when the global row is newer, so an Owner editing a global default cannot silently override a deliberate per-branch value. EXECUTE granted to NOBODY (config_settings holds prices; R20 keeps L3 out), and since ^ref-64 the grant is no longer the only enforcement — the body raises NO_ACTOR when auth.uid() is null, because ADR-004's "RLS decides" does not reach inside a SECURITY DEFINER function.

nodes.label: fn_config_numeric
nodes.rationale: Thin typed wrapper over fn_config_value for the column almost every call site wants. Raises CONFIG_WRONG_TYPE when a text or jsonb key is asked for as a number, because a null rate is the same failure CONFIG_NOT_SET exists to stop, one step further downstream. NO_ACTOR is inherited, not repeated — the fn_config_value call is the first statement of the body, so one guard in one place. EXECUTE granted to nobody: a primitive for definer functions, not a read path.

nodes.label: fn_confirm_transport_receipt
nodes.rationale: Card ^ref-22 / D06, UAT-11, BR12, R22: the receiving side signs for what actually arrived. A partial receipt is not an error — the shortfall stays honestly in IN_TRANSIT and partial_receipt_allowed (per-location config) decides whether it may be recorded at all. The TRANSFER_IN posts the RECEIVED weight, never the dispatched one, or the function would conjure the shortfall into the destination's stock; the one exception is an over-delivery, where least() clears only what went onto the truck (drawing more is refused by fn_post_ledger's non-negative guard, R3/BR24) and the surplus is posted as an ADJUSTMENT carrying the receiver's reason, because calling it TRANSFER_IN would say meat travelled on a truck that never carried it. Mode is ALERT, never BLOCK: a receipt is a fact that already happened and refusing it does not make the meat reappear. The verdict comes from fn_check_variance and never from transport_lines.variance_pct, which rounds to 4 decimals and compares raw — they disagree at 20.004% and one line cannot have two verdicts (TC-21). p_event_date is a parameter because the run's event_date is the DISPATCH date and both config lookups plus the ledger business_date need the receipt's own date (R12). Role comes from the DESTINATION location kind, not from an argument. The receipt carries its own second idempotency key under `select ... for update`, which is what makes two concurrent receipts resolve to one winner and one named refusal rather than two TRANSFER_IN rows (TC-41). Arriving stock lands FROZEN, not READY, because R14 moves weight FROZEN -> READY at the branch.

nodes.label: fn_create_po
nodes.rationale: Card ^ref-19: the Owner raises a purchase order against a supplier. A PO is a COMMITMENT, not a movement — nothing here touches stock_ledger, because the meat has not left Foodiva and stock enters at fn_dispatch_transport_line (TC-25 counts the ledger and asserts it did not move). ordered_weight_kg is never the loss base; what actually left the building is recorded per round on po_deliveries (BR03, R16). po_number is generated (PO-YYYYMM-NNN) rather than typed, with the counter derived under a pg_advisory_xact_lock on the month — the xact form, never the session form, which leaks into the next request on a pooled connection — and from max() of the existing suffix rather than count(*), so a gap cannot hand out a number already written on paper. created_by is resolved from auth.uid() inside the body and is never a parameter, so a caller cannot sign a purchase commitment as somebody else (TC-06). R4 idempotency: same key + same payload replays the original id; same key + different payload raises PO_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT rather than reporting a 120 kg order that does not exist. L1-only is checked in the body because SECURITY DEFINER means RLS does not apply inside it — the function is the boundary (ADR-002, ADR-004). No audit_log insert here; ^ref-06's trigger already writes one in the same transaction (TC-26).

nodes.label: fn_create_transport_run
nodes.rationale: Card ^ref-22 / M2, BR16, D04.1: creates the vehicle, its fare and the method that will split that fare — and no lines. The p_lot_ids array is taken, checked and discarded so R26 can be asked ONCE over the whole array at run creation rather than per line after three lines already exist (TC-10): a CM_TO_FOODIVA run is refused unless every lot on it is RETURN_SCHEDULED, which is what BR17 means by the return leg existing only once someone entitled to do so has named a receive date. alloc_method is SNAPSHOTTED here from dated config and is not a parameter (R29, BR23): a caller who can choose the method can choose differently for two runs on the same day, and more importantly fn_allocate_freight reads the method off this row so a later config change cannot move a closed number. CONFIG_NOT_SET propagates rather than defaulting (ADR-023). R25's branch-leg-carries-no-fare is raised by name as well as enforced by transport_runs_branch_leg_free, so an Owner reads a rule rather than a constraint name. R4 idempotency mirrors fn_add_po_delivery, including the unique_violation fallback where the losing session reads the winner's row.

nodes.label: fn_current_locations
nodes.rationale: Returns the locations the caller may touch as a uuid[]. SECURITY DEFINER for fn_current_role()'s reason: a policy on user_locations must be able to call it without re-entering itself. Returns '{}' and never null — `x = any(null)` is null, which a policy happens to read as false, and an empty array makes that the right answer by construction rather than by luck. Folds in profiles.is_active (R31), so a deactivated profile touches nothing. can_receive_central is deliberately NOT read here (R27, BR12, BR17): that delegation grants the act of receiving, not extra read scope, and whichever fn_* implements the act checks the column itself.

nodes.label: fn_current_role()
nodes.rationale: SECURITY DEFINER for correctness, not hardening: a policy on profiles calling this would re-enter profiles own policy and recurse. Folds is_active in so a deactivated profile with a live JWT resolves to null, which every policy reads as false. Standing rule: never FORCE RLS on a table a helper reads.

nodes.label: fn_require_owner()
nodes.rationale: Shared preamble for every L1-only write. Order is the behaviour: actor first (NO_ACTOR, R31), then role (FORBIDDEN, ADR-004), because fn_current_role goes null for a deactivated Owner. Returns created_by so a caller cannot sign a row as somebody else. EXECUTE granted to nobody.

nodes.label: fn_require_branch(location)
nodes.rationale: L2 counterpart of fn_require_owner, kept separate so L1-only setters never inherit the branch arm. Three checks: actor, L2 role, location membership. Step 3 is not redundant with step 2 in either direction: L3 also holds user_locations rows, and an L2 at branch A must not open branch B. L1 is refused deliberately. EXECUTE granted to nobody.

nodes.label: fn_post_ledger()
nodes.rationale: The ONLY writer of stock_ledger (ADR-002, ADR-005). Idempotency is a RETURN, not a raise (R4). The non-negative balance check is serialised by a TRANSACTION-scoped advisory lock on the balance tuple taken before the SUM; pg_advisory_lock would leak the lock into the next pooled connection. Every SMOKED_MEAT movement must name its lot (R21/ADR-017). Deliberately writes no audit row, because the generic trigger already fires in the same transaction.

nodes.label: fn_reverse_ledger_entry()
nodes.rationale: The only correction path (ADR-003, R2): a REVERSAL row plus a replacement row, never an edit. The replacement key is derived md5(caller_key + ":replacement") so a retry re-derives it and both inserts hit ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. L1 only, checked inside because SECURITY DEFINER bypasses RLS. Already-reversed is checked against the ledger, not a mutable flag column.

nodes.label: fn_record_opening_balance()
nodes.rationale: The only path creating stock with no PO behind it, and nothing to check itself against. HAS NO COST PARAMETER OF ANY KIND (BR15/R20): a price that cannot be passed cannot be leaked by an L3 screen. L1 IS NOT A SUPERSET HERE (ADR-021), each role counts only its own kind of location, because a count is a physical act. Stock state is derived, not a parameter: meat lands FROZEN. Meat needs a lot and a smoke date or FIFO silently sorts it newest and the oldest meat never leaves.

nodes.label: fn_set_opening_cost()
nodes.rationale: The L1 half of the opening flow, a separate function precisely so "who may enter a price" is answered by which function you may call rather than by a branch inside a body. Upserts on ledger_id and refuses any ledger row whose movement_type is not OPENING.

nodes.label: fn_dispatch_transport_line()
nodes.rationale: Posts the transport leg: a TRANSFER_OUT draw at the origin under a derived ":out" key, and a matching IN_TRANSIT row held at the destination. A FOODIVA_TO_CM line has no origin location because the supplier is not one of ours; every other route must name one. Idempotency compares the whole payload and raises LINE_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT if the key was reused for a different line.

nodes.label: fn_open_daily_report()
nodes.rationale: Opens a branch shift, L2 only via fn_require_branch. One OPEN report per branch is enforced by a unique index and surfaced as REPORT_STILL_OPEN (BR21, R13). Reopening a closed day is the unlock path, not this function (R28). Carries yesterday cooked rice forward in the response.

nodes.label: fn_set_config()
nodes.rationale: Dated config writer (ADR-006, R12). Exactly one of numeric/text/json. A same-key same-date write with an identical value returns the existing id as a retry; a different value raises CONFIG_DUPLICATE_DATE, because append-only has no same-day correction (BR23).

nodes.label: fn_set_product_price()
nodes.rationale: Dated price writer under the same append-only same-day rule as fn_set_config (BR23). A retry returns the existing row only when price and cost both match.

nodes.label: fn_set_packaging_full_stock()
nodes.rationale: Dated full-stock level writer. Takes an advisory xact lock on (item, location, date) before the read-then-insert because no unique constraint covers the nullable location. Refuses zero: "not configured" is the absence of a row, not a zero row (R9).

nodes.label: fn_set_smoke_fee_tier()
nodes.rationale: Writes a whole band set as one dated unit (D02, R37). Validates that the set is anchored at 0, has no gap and no overlap, and that the top band is open-ended so a heavier dispatch cannot fall off the table. An identical set at the same date returns the band count as a retry; a different one raises CONFIG_DUPLICATE_DATE.

nodes.label: v_stock_balance
nodes.rationale: Balance is SUM(qty_delta) over the ledger, never a stored column. Row visibility lives in the WHERE: L1 everything, L2 only their own locations, L3 nothing.

nodes.label: v_smoke_group_available
nodes.rationale: FIFO picker source: smoke groups holding a positive balance, ordered smoke_date then lot.

nodes.label: v_po_outstanding
nodes.rationale: UAT-01. Dispatched and outstanding derive from po_deliveries; received_weight_kg is a CM cross-check only (R16a). The loss base and yield divisor is lots.foodiva_sent_weight_kg (BR03, ADR-011). L1 only, enforced in the WHERE (R34).

nodes.label: v_audit_trail
nodes.rationale: OW 11. One row per CHANGED FIELD of an UPDATE. changed_at is audit_log.created_at, never event_date (ADR-007). L1 only in the WHERE; audit_log itself stays deny-all.

nodes.label: v_config_history
nodes.rationale: OW 10. Unions config_settings, product_prices, packaging_full_stock and smoke_fee_tiers into one shape. is_current orders the way fn_config_value orders (ADR-006, R12) and a future row is never current. A smoke-fee band set is ONE row (D02, R37). L1 only; the four tables stay deny-all.

nodes.label: v_config_catalogue
nodes.rationale: OW 10 pickers: ids and names only, no rate, price or quantity. Active rows only. L1 only via the WHERE (R34); the three tables stay deny-all (ADR-004).

nodes.label: v_freight_allocation
nodes.rationale: R24. Per-line freight share, the snapshotted allocation method (R29), and whether the run shares still sum back to its fare to the satang. L1 only (R34, R20).

nodes.label: v_transport_variance
nodes.rationale: UAT-11/BR12. variance_pct is fn_check_variance figure (ADR-019), never transport_lines.variance_pct: the two disagree at the third decimal. No verdict column, because a dated threshold needs fn_config_numeric which no session may execute (R20). L1 all, L2 either end of their own branch, L3 their assigned lots.

nodes.label: v_outstanding_receipts
nodes.rationale: D06. Lines never signed for, plus partial receipts that left a balance in IN_TRANSIT. age_days derives from transport_lines.created_at. L1 all, L2 either end of their own branch, L3 nothing.

nodes.label: user_role (enum)
nodes.rationale: The three-role boundary L1_OWNER / L2_BRANCH_ADMIN / L3_CM_OPERATOR is a database-level type, not a UI concept (ADR-004).

nodes.label: lot_state (enum)
nodes.rationale: Encodes the whole dispatch-to-consumption lifecycle: PO_CREATED through IN_TRANSIT, CM_RECEIVED, SMOKING, LOT_CLOSED, RETURN_SCHEDULED, CENTRAL_STOCK, ALLOCATED, AT_BRANCH, CONSUMED.

nodes.label: movement_type (enum)
nodes.rationale: Signed-delta vocabulary for the append-only ledger; REVERSAL exists because ADR-003 forbids UPDATE/DELETE, so a correction must be a new row.

nodes.label: report_status (enum)
nodes.rationale: OPEN / CLOSED / UNLOCKED — UNLOCKED is a past day reopened under R28/ADR-013 and must be distinguishable from today's OPEN day.

nodes.label: profiles (table)
nodes.rationale: Application identity keyed 1:1 to auth.users, carrying the role that RLS decides on. Cascade delete keeps it in step with the auth row.

nodes.label: locations (table)
nodes.rationale: One table for CENTRAL, CHEF_HOUSE and BRANCH so every ledger row can name where stock sits.

nodes.label: locations_rice_model_branch_only (check constraint)
nodes.rationale: A rice model only means anything for a branch; central and chef house must leave it null.

nodes.label: user_locations (table)
nodes.rationale: BR12/BR17 delegation: can_receive_central grants the ACT of receiving, not visibility of the data behind it.

nodes.label: smoke_fee_tiers (table)
nodes.rationale: Dated weight bands for the smoke fee (ADR-006/ADR-018): the rate is resolved by event date, never a constant in code.

nodes.label: smoke_fee_tiers_band (check constraint)
nodes.rationale: A band must be non-degenerate: max weight is either null (open-ended top band) or strictly above the minimum.

nodes.label: config_settings (table)
nodes.rationale: ADR-006: every business number lives here, dated and optionally scoped to a location; resolution is (key, scope, effective_from <= event_date) desc limit 1.

nodes.label: config_settings_one_value (check constraint)
nodes.rationale: Exactly one of value_numeric / value_text / value_json is set, so a config row has one unambiguous reading.

nodes.label: config_settings_key_scope_date (unique index)
nodes.rationale: Coalesces a null scope to a sentinel uuid so global and per-location rows share one unique key per effective date; this natural key also carries config-write idempotency without a key column.

nodes.label: unlock_requests (table)
nodes.rationale: R28/ADR-013 reopen path: a closed report or lot is reopened only through a requested, decided and expiring approval, never silently.

nodes.label: audit_log (table)
nodes.rationale: Generic before/after trail carrying actor, role, event_date and idempotency_key so a disputed back-dated write can be reconciled.

nodes.label: notifications (table)
nodes.rationale: lot_id is declared here without its FK because lots does not exist yet in the chain; the constraint is added in migration ...0003.

nodes.label: purchase_orders (table)
nodes.rationale: Head of the purchasing chain; po_number is unique but generated inside fn_create_po, which is why it cannot serve as a retry key (see ...0008).

nodes.label: po_deliveries (table)
nodes.rationale: foodiva_sent_weight_kg here is THE loss base and the smoke-fee tier base (BR03/BR10, ADR-011) — never the Chiang Mai received weight.

nodes.label: lots (table)
nodes.rationale: D01: one delivery round, one lot — po_delivery_id is UNIQUE. return_pickup_date gates the return run (BR17): closing a lot creates no transport job on its own.

nodes.label: notifications_lot_id_fkey (foreign key)
nodes.rationale: Deferred FK: notifications was created before lots existed, so the constraint is attached here once the target table is in place.

nodes.label: lot_receipts (table)
nodes.rationale: R16a: received_weight_kg is a CROSS-CHECK only and never the loss base; the divisor stays the Foodiva dispatch weight (ADR-011).

nodes.label: smoke_daily_logs (table)
nodes.rationale: R6: one log per lot per day. input_weight_kg is a trigger-maintained roll-up of its sources (R6a), never typed directly.

nodes.label: smoke_daily_log_sources (table)
nodes.rationale: D05: one smoking day may draw input from several lots, so each contributing lot gets its own row and the parent sums them.

nodes.label: fn_rollup_smoke_log_input() (trigger function)
nodes.rationale: R6a: keeps the parent input weight equal to the sum of its source rows so the two can never disagree.

nodes.label: smoke_date_groups (table)
nodes.rationale: R7: the FIFO unit — one group per lot per smoke date, so a branch quantity traces back to a smoke-date group and then to a lot.

nodes.label: transport_runs (table)
nodes.rationale: alloc_method is snapshotted on the run (BR16) so a later config change cannot retroactively re-split freight already booked.

nodes.label: transport_runs_branch_leg_free (check constraint)
nodes.rationale: R25/BR11: a CENTRAL_TO_BRANCH run carries no fare, so run_cost_thb must be zero on that route.

nodes.label: transport_lines (table)
nodes.rationale: D06 outstanding_weight_kg and BR12 variance_pct are generated columns; variance_pct is a sort key only, because the threshold verdict belongs to fn_check_variance (ADR-019), which rounds before comparing.

nodes.label: products (table)
nodes.rationale: is_stock_tracked is false for items like drinks that are sold but never enter the ledger.

nodes.label: product_prices (table)
nodes.rationale: BR23: prices are dated rows, unique per (product, effective_from); cost_thb is null where the cost comes from the lot instead.

nodes.label: packaging_full_stock (table)
nodes.rationale: R9: full_stock_qty must be strictly positive because zero would mean 'not configured' and is used as a divisor for the low-material alert.

nodes.label: daily_reports (table)
nodes.rationale: BR22/ADR-014: report_date is the BUSINESS date. A 01:00 entry attaches to the branch's still-open report and so belongs to the previous day; R5 makes (location, date) unique.

nodes.label: sales_lines (table)
nodes.rationale: unit_price_thb is a BR23 snapshot taken at sale time; lot_id is nullable in DDL but forced non-null for SMOKED_MEAT by a trigger (R21).

nodes.label: thaw_records (table)
nodes.rationale: R15: fifo_override_reason records why the operator skipped the oldest smoke-date group.

nodes.label: fn_require_lot_for_meat() (trigger function)
nodes.rationale: R21/D01: every meat movement must name its source lot. Shared by sales_lines and waste_records; it resolves item_type from products for sales and from the row itself for waste.

nodes.label: physical_counts (table)
nodes.rationale: system_qty is snapshotted at count time and variance_qty is generated from it, so the count's verdict cannot drift as later ledger rows land.

nodes.label: rice_records (table)
nodes.rationale: Two rice models in one table (M7A external-cooked, M7B self-cook); the price columns are L1-only under BR15.

nodes.label: stock_ledger (table)
nodes.rationale: ADR-003: the only stock table. Append-only, signed qty_delta, no balance column anywhere — balance is SUM(qty_delta). Carries all three clocks (business_date, event_at, created_at, ADR-007), a unique idempotency_key (R4/ADR-005) and reversal_of for R2 corrections.

nodes.label: fn_stock_ledger_append_only() (trigger function)
nodes.rationale: R1: raises unconditionally. It never inspects a row, which is why it is attached as a statement-level trigger.

nodes.label: trg_stock_ledger_append_only (trigger)
nodes.rationale: Refuses every UPDATE and DELETE on stock_ledger; corrections must be a REVERSAL row plus a replacement (R1/R2).

nodes.label: owner_expenses (table)
nodes.rationale: expense_month is text constrained to YYYY-MM (M11.5) for monthly fixed costs; a null location_id means central.

nodes.label: attendance (table)
nodes.rationale: unique (staff_id, event_date) makes one attendance verdict per person per day.

nodes.label: RLS deny-all bootstrap (DO block)
nodes.rationale: ADR-002/ADR-004: loops every public table, enables RLS and revokes all from anon and authenticated. RLS on with no policy is deny-all, which is the intended posture until the fn_* writers and v_* views exist.

nodes.label: Function search_path hardening
nodes.rationale: Supabase linter 0011/0028/0029: pins search_path = public, pg_temp on the three trigger functions so a hostile schema on the caller's path cannot shadow their table references.

nodes.label: rls_auto_enable() revoke guard
nodes.rationale: Revokes EXECUTE from anon/authenticated on a pre-existing helper that lives in the live project but in none of these files; guarded by to_regprocedure so a fresh database does not abort the migration chain.

nodes.label: trg_stock_ledger_no_truncate (trigger)
nodes.rationale: Closes the TRUNCATE hole in R1/ADR-003: TRUNCATE fires neither UPDATE nor DELETE, so the one statement that empties the whole ledger went straight past the original guard. Postgres needs a separate BEFORE TRUNCATE statement trigger, reusing the same raising function.

nodes.label: purchase_orders_idempotency_key (unique index + column)
nodes.rationale: R4/ADR-005 needs a client-generated retry key and po_number cannot serve: it is minted inside fn_create_po, so a replay mints a second number and a second PO and the existing unique index never fires. Nullable because the writer rejects a null key before writing.

nodes.label: po_deliveries_idempotency_key (unique index + column)
nodes.rationale: (po_id, seq) cannot carry the retry because seq is derived as max(seq)+1, so a replay books a second round and every lot, freight share and yield figure downstream inherits it. A payload key on (po_id, event_date, weight) is worse: two genuine same-day rounds are ordinary and would be refused (TC-24).

nodes.label: daily_reports_one_open (unique partial index)
nodes.rationale: THE implementation of ADR-014: exactly one OPEN report per branch is what makes a 01:00 entry land on the previous day — the open row is the business-day boundary, not a clock. The predicate must be status = 'OPEN', never status <> 'CLOSED', so an UNLOCKED past day (R28/ADR-013) can coexist with today.

nodes.label: transport_runs_idempotency_key (unique index + column)
nodes.rationale: A run has no unique business key at all — two FOODIVA_TO_CM runs on the same date with the same vehicle type is ordinary — so R4's retry key needs its own column.

nodes.label: transport_lines_idempotency_key (unique index + column)
nodes.rationale: The dispatch half of R4. Without it a replayed fn_dispatch_transport_line posts a second TRANSFER_OUT and a 40 kg dispatch becomes 80 kg stuck in IN_TRANSIT against a lot that can never balance. (run_id, lot_id) cannot stand in: a lot may ride one run twice when split across smoke date groups.

nodes.label: transport_lines_receipt_idempotency_key (unique index + column)
nodes.rationale: A line is written twice by two different callers, so it carries two keys; sharing one would make the receipt look like a replayed dispatch. It is also what makes TC-41 deterministic — the loser of a concurrent confirm sees the key already set and raises LINE_ALREADY_RECEIVED.

nodes.label: movement_type value 'OPENING'
nodes.rationale: Alone in its own migration for two independent reasons: `alter type ... add value` cannot be rolled back, and the new value cannot be USED in the transaction that added it (migration ...0012 writes a trigger predicate on it). A distinct value rather than ADJUSTMENT-with-a-reason (ADR-021) so the close switch is a trigger predicate instead of a LIKE on free text, and so corrections stay separable from the opening position.

nodes.label: lots_round_or_opening (check constraint)
nodes.rationale: A BICONDITIONAL, not a disjunction: either a lot has its whole purchasing history (po_id, po_delivery_id, dispatch weight, chef house) or it has none of it. A disjunction would readmit the rejected synthetic-round design — an opening lot carrying a phantom PO. D01 is untouched: po_delivery_id stays UNIQUE; it never said a lot must have a round.

nodes.label: opening_balance_close (table)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately NOT a config key: config_settings resolution is dated, so a permanent switch stored there is reopenable by writing a later effective_from and fn_set_config would do it without noticing. `id boolean primary key check (id)` is the single-row idiom — empty means the window is open, one row means closed, and a second close is a key violation rather than a rule someone must remember. closed_idempotency_key separates a genuine retry (returns the original closed_at, R4) from a deliberate second close (OPENING_ALREADY_CLOSED, TC-29).

nodes.label: opening_costs (table)
nodes.rationale: R46 wants a cost per kg on every OPENING row while BR15 forbids the counter seeing a price, so quantity and cost are entered by different people at different times — an UPDATE, which trg_stock_ledger_append_only refuses. Putting the column on stock_ledger would mean relaxing R1 for one column, a hole in ADR-003. The primary key on ledger_id also makes fn_set_opening_cost idempotent with no key column, and lets the close check for a MISSING ROW by left join instead of a null column.

nodes.label: fn_stock_ledger_opening_closed() (trigger function)
nodes.rationale: Deliberate duplication of fn_record_opening_balance's check: the function gives a screen a legible Thai error, this trigger makes ADR-021's 'by anyone, ever' true — including a write function added in 2027 that calls fn_post_ledger directly. BEFORE INSERT FOR EACH ROW because it must read new.movement_type, and the subquery runs only for OPENING rows so the ordinary ledger path pays one enum comparison.

nodes.label: attendance RLS posture (deny-all, provisional)
nodes.rationale: No CREATE POLICY exists: RLS is enabled and all grants revoked from anon/authenticated, so no role can read or write the table directly. Reads must arrive through a role-specific SECURITY DEFINER v_* view and writes only through a SECURITY DEFINER fn_* (ADR-002, ADR-004) — the three-role boundary (L1 Owner / L2 Branch Admin / L3 CM Operator) is decided in the database, never in the UI. Placeholder posture: the SELECT policy lands here when the card owning its view is written.

nodes.label: audit_log RLS posture (deny-all, FINAL)
nodes.rationale: FINAL deny-all, not a placeholder (card ^ref-09). No SELECT policy will ever land: v_audit_trail is SECURITY DEFINER and bypasses RLS, and fn_audit_row is SECURITY DEFINER for the same reason. A SELECT policy here would open a second read path around the view's L1-Owner-only WHERE clause, breaking the role boundary that the audit screen depends on (ADR-002, ADR-004).

nodes.label: branch_expenses RLS posture (deny-all, provisional)
nodes.rationale: Deny-all until a role-specific v_* view exists. Branch expenses are money rows scoped to an L2 Branch Admin's own branch; until that scoping lives in a view, no session reads the table directly (ADR-002, ADR-004).

nodes.label: config_settings RLS posture (deny-all, FINAL)
nodes.rationale: FINAL deny-all (card ^ref-12). NO SELECT POLICY LANDS: reads arrive only through v_config_history, which is SECURITY DEFINER and carries `where fn_current_role() = 'L1_OWNER'` (R34, R20). A table policy would be a second read path around that WHERE, reachable by any session that types the table name into PostgREST — it would leak dated business numbers (prices, rates, targets) to L2 and L3. Standing consequence: never `force row level security` on this table or on profiles, or the owner-run view returns nothing even for L1.

nodes.label: daily_reports RLS posture (deny-all, provisional)
nodes.rationale: Deny-all until a role-specific v_* view exists; reads through the view, writes through a SECURITY DEFINER fn_* only (ADR-002, ADR-004).

nodes.label: influencer_shipments RLS posture (deny-all, provisional)
nodes.rationale: Deny-all until a role-specific v_* view exists; reads through the view, writes through a SECURITY DEFINER fn_* only (ADR-002, ADR-004).

nodes.label: locations RLS posture (deny-all, provisional)
nodes.rationale: Deny-all until a role-specific v_* view exists. Location visibility is the spine of the L2 branch boundary (a branch admin sees only their own locations), so it is decided in a view under the database's control, not in the UI (ADR-004).

nodes.label: lot_bags RLS posture (deny-all, provisional)
nodes.rationale: Deny-all until a role-specific v_* view exists; reads through the view, writes through a SECURITY DEFINER fn_* only (ADR-002, ADR-004).

nodes.label: lot_receipts RLS posture (deny-all, provisional)
nodes.rationale: Deny-all until a role-specific v_* view exists; reads through the view, writes through a SECURITY DEFINER fn_* only (ADR-002, ADR-004).

nodes.label: lots RLS posture (deny-all, provisional)
nodes.rationale: Deny-all until a role-specific v_* view exists. A lot row carries cost and yield figures an L3 CM Operator must never read, so no direct table read is granted; a per-role view decides which columns each role sees (ADR-004, R20).

nodes.label: notifications RLS posture (deny-all, provisional)
nodes.rationale: Deny-all until a role-specific v_* view exists; reads through the view, writes through a SECURITY DEFINER fn_* only (ADR-002, ADR-004).

nodes.label: opening_balance_close RLS posture (deny-all, no DELETE path)
nodes.rationale: Deny-all until a role-specific v_* exists; ^ref-61's v_config_readiness reads it as a WARN row while the table is empty. Beyond the role boundary this posture is half of an immutability guarantee: there is no DELETE path anywhere in the repo and there must not be one — the deny-all revoke is one half, no fn_* deleting from it is the other (ADR-021). Sweep 1a of rls_deny_all_test.sql catches the posture's absence.
nodes.norm_label: opening_balance_close rls posture (deny-all, no delete path)

nodes.label: opening_costs RLS posture (deny-all, load-bearing for L3 price-blindness)
nodes.rationale: Deny-all, and R20 makes it load-bearing rather than provisional: this table holds a price, and the L3 CM Operator is exactly the person who counts the meat that price belongs to. BR15 keeps the price out of fn_record_opening_balance's signature (write side); this posture keeps it out of any SELECT (read side). Column-level price restriction enforced by denying the table outright. Sweep 1a of rls_deny_all_test.sql catches its absence.
nodes.norm_label: opening_costs rls posture (deny-all, load-bearing for l3 price-blindness)

nodes.label: owner_expenses RLS posture (deny-all, provisional)
nodes.rationale: Deny-all until a role-specific v_* view exists. Owner expenses are L1-only money rows; neither L2 nor L3 reaches them, and that is decided in the database, not the UI (ADR-004).

nodes.label: packaging_full_stock RLS posture (deny-all, FINAL)
nodes.rationale: FINAL deny-all (card ^ref-12). NO SELECT POLICY LANDS: reads arrive only through v_config_history, SECURITY DEFINER, carrying `where fn_current_role() = 'L1_OWNER'` (R34, R20). A table policy would be a second read path around that WHERE, reachable from PostgREST by any session, exposing owner-only configuration to L2 and L3. Never `force row level security` here or on profiles — the owner-run view would then return nothing, L1 included.

nodes.label: packaging_items RLS posture (deny-all, provisional)
nodes.rationale: Deny-all until a role-specific v_* view exists; reads through the view, writes through a SECURITY DEFINER fn_* only (ADR-002, ADR-004).

nodes.label: physical_counts RLS posture (deny-all, provisional)
nodes.rationale: Deny-all until a role-specific v_* view exists. Counts are entered by L3 and L2 but valued in money only for L1, so the read shape is a per-role view rather than a table grant (ADR-004, R20).

nodes.label: po_deliveries RLS posture (deny-all, provisional)
nodes.rationale: Deny-all until a role-specific v_* view exists. Delivery rows carry supplier cost, which an L3 session must never read; no table grant is issued (ADR-004, R20).

nodes.label: product_prices RLS posture (deny-all, FINAL)
nodes.rationale: FINAL deny-all (card ^ref-12). NO SELECT POLICY LANDS: reads arrive only through v_config_history, SECURITY DEFINER, carrying `where fn_current_role() = 'L1_OWNER'` (R34, R20). This is the purest case of L3 price-blindness — the table is nothing but dated prices, so any table-level policy would be a second read path around the owner-only WHERE and would hand prices to L2 and L3 through PostgREST. Never `force row level security` here or on profiles.

nodes.label: rls_deny_all_test (posture sweeps, ^ref-64)
nodes.rationale: Seven read-only catalogue sweeps proving the ADR-004 deny-all posture, runnable against the live project via migrations_apply_test.sh --db-url. 1a every public table has RLS on; 1b anon holds nothing on any table or view; 1c authenticated holds no write privilege; 1d a table authenticated can SELECT carries a SELECT policy; 1e anon holds EXECUTE on no function in public; 1f the seven no-grant functions (fn_audit_row, fn_audit_log_append_only, fn_stock_ledger_append_only, fn_stock_ledger_opening_closed, fn_require_lot_for_meat, fn_rollup_smoke_log_input and peers) are executable by neither role, by name; 1g every other fn_* is executable by authenticated and not by anon. FINDING that motivated ^ref-64: pg_default_acl in a Supabase project grants to anon and authenticated BY NAME, and `revoke ... from public` does not remove a named-role grant — so every revoke in the repo was real in Docker and inert live, leaving 1b/1c green over 22 open function grants. Docker has no default ACLs and structurally cannot see it.

nodes.label: Policy profiles_select_self_or_owner
nodes.rationale: The only live SELECT policy in the RLS set. Encodes the three-role boundary: a caller sees their own row (id = auth.uid()), an L1 Owner sees everyone; L2 Branch Admin and L3 CM Operator reading another user get zero rows rather than an error (UAT-15 / TC-05). The leading `fn_current_role() is not null` guard is the deactivated-caller refusal (TC-07) and is written on the caller, not on the row's is_active, so the Owner can still manage deactivated rows. Granting SELECT here is safe under the L3 price/yield rule (R20) only because profiles carries no price and no yield column - just display_name, role, is_active. Writes stay revoked forever: role and is_active change through a SECURITY DEFINER fn_* (ADR-002). Never `force row level security` on profiles - that removes the owner's RLS bypass and fn_current_role() would re-enter this policy.

nodes.label: profiles RLS posture (SELECT granted, writes revoked)
nodes.rationale: The one exception to deny-all: `grant select on public.profiles to authenticated`, all other privileges revoked from anon and authenticated. Column-level safety by table shape - no price, no yield column - is what makes the grant compatible with the L3 read restriction.

nodes.label: products RLS posture (deny-all)
nodes.rationale: RLS enabled with no policy and all privileges revoked from anon and authenticated - a table with RLS on and zero policies denies every row. Placeholder posture: the SELECT policy lands only when the card owning the role-specific v_* view is written. Reads arrive through the view, writes only through a SECURITY DEFINER fn_* (ADR-002, ADR-004). Declared per-table because migration ...0005 looped over pg_tables at its own migration time and cannot cover tables created later.

nodes.label: purchase_orders RLS posture (deny-all)
nodes.rationale: RLS enabled with no policy plus a full revoke from anon and authenticated: deny-all. Purchase orders carry supplier price columns, so leaving this closed is also what keeps an L3 CM Operator session away from price data (R20) until a role-specific view exists (ADR-002, ADR-004).

nodes.label: rice_records RLS posture (deny-all)
nodes.rationale: RLS enabled with no policy and privileges revoked from anon and authenticated - deny-all until the card owning the role-specific v_* view lands a SELECT policy. Reads through the view, writes through a SECURITY DEFINER fn_* (ADR-002, ADR-004).

nodes.label: sales_lines RLS posture (deny-all)

Sale lines carry selling prices, so the closed posture is also the current enforcement of the rule that an L3 session never reads a price column (R20), and of the branch-visibility boundary an L2 view will later narrow (ADR-004).

nodes.label: smoke_daily_log_sources RLS posture (deny-all)
nodes.rationale: RLS enabled with no policy and privileges revoked from anon and authenticated - deny-all until the owning card writes the role-specific view. Reads through the view, writes only through a SECURITY DEFINER fn_* (ADR-002, ADR-004).

nodes.label: smoke_daily_logs RLS posture (deny-all)
nodes.rationale: RLS enabled with no policy plus a full revoke: deny-all. Smoke logs are the table an L3 CM Operator writes against but whose yield figures L3 must not read (R20), so no SELECT policy lands here - the split happens in the role-specific view (ADR-002, ADR-004).

nodes.label: smoke_date_groups RLS posture (deny-all)
nodes.rationale: RLS enabled with no policy and privileges revoked from anon and authenticated - deny-all until the card owning the role-specific v_* view is written. Reads through the view, writes through a SECURITY DEFINER fn_* (ADR-002, ADR-004).

nodes.label: smoke_fee_tiers RLS posture (final deny-all, no policy ever)
nodes.rationale: Final, not a placeholder (card ^ref-12): NO SELECT POLICY EVER LANDS. Reads arrive only through v_config_history, which is SECURITY DEFINER and carries `where fn_current_role() = 'L1_OWNER'` (R34, R20) - a policy on the table would be a second read path around that WHERE, reachable by any session that types the table name into PostgREST. Fee tiers are price data, so the single door is what keeps an L2 or L3 session out. Standing consequence: never `force row level security` on this table or on profiles, because the view runs as the owner and forcing RLS would make it return nothing, for L1 too. Writes only via a SECURITY DEFINER fn_set_* (ADR-002, ADR-004).

nodes.label: staff RLS posture (deny-all)

nodes.label: stock_ledger RLS posture (deny-all)
nodes.rationale: RLS enabled with no policy plus `revoke all` from anon and authenticated - deny-all, and with no UPDATE or DELETE policy the append-only ledger rule (ADR-003) holds by construction: no client session can rewrite or remove a ledger row, and corrections must arrive as a reversal row plus a replacement row through a SECURITY DEFINER fn_*. Balance is SUM(qty_delta) over these rows, never a mutable column. Reads land later through a role-specific v_* view (ADR-002, ADR-004).

nodes.label: suppliers RLS posture (deny-all)
nodes.rationale: RLS enabled with no policy and privileges revoked from anon and authenticated - deny-all until the card owning the role-specific v_* view lands a SELECT policy. Reads through the view, writes through a SECURITY DEFINER fn_* (ADR-002, ADR-004).

nodes.label: thaw_records RLS posture (deny-all)
nodes.rationale: RLS enabled with no policy and a full revoke from anon and authenticated - deny-all. Thaw records are L3 CM Operator territory for writes, but writes go through a SECURITY DEFINER fn_*, never a direct grant (ADR-002, ADR-004).

nodes.label: transport_lines RLS posture (deny-all)
nodes.rationale: RLS enabled with no policy plus a full revoke: deny-all. Transport lines carry the freight cost split, a price column an L3 session must not read (R20), so no SELECT policy lands until the role-specific view exists (ADR-002, ADR-004).

nodes.label: transport_runs RLS posture (deny-all)
nodes.rationale: RLS enabled with no policy and privileges revoked from anon and authenticated - deny-all. Freight totals on a run are price data, kept behind a role-specific view rather than a table policy (ADR-002, ADR-004, R20).

nodes.label: unlock_requests RLS posture (deny-all)
nodes.rationale: RLS enabled with no policy and a full revoke from anon and authenticated - deny-all. An unlock request is the L2/L3 escalation path to an L1 Owner approval, so both the raise and the approve are SECURITY DEFINER fn_* calls rather than table grants; the role check lives in the function and the view, not in the UI (ADR-002, ADR-004).

nodes.label: user_locations RLS posture (deny-all)
nodes.rationale: RLS enabled with no policy plus a full revoke: deny-all. user_locations is the mapping an L2 Branch Admin's visibility is derived from, so it is read by SECURITY DEFINER helpers rather than exposed to authenticated sessions - the same recursion-avoidance shape profiles needs (ADR-002, ADR-004).

nodes.label: waste_records RLS posture (deny-all)
nodes.rationale: RLS enabled with no policy and privileges revoked from anon and authenticated - deny-all until the role-specific v_* view is written. Waste rows value the loss, so the price side stays behind the view (ADR-002, ADR-004, R20).

nodes.label: audit_trail_test (card ^ref-09)
nodes.rationale: Failure-case suite for v_audit_trail, the OW 11 reader. TC-A/TC-B: an L3 and an L2 session each read 0 rows (role gate in the database, not the nav, ADR-004). TC-C: the Owner still reads rows, so 'deny everyone' cannot pass the deny tests vacuously. TC-D: a one-field UPDATE expands to exactly one row with field_name/old_value/new_value correct and actor_name joined from profiles. TC-E: an INSERT is one event with a null field_name, not one row per column. TC-F: an authenticated session is refused a direct read of audit_log, can still select the view, and no anon/authenticated grant was added on the table. TC-G: changed_at is audit_log.created_at, not the audited row's created_at and not the business event_date (ADR-007). Covers failure cases, not only the happy path.

nodes.label: audit_trigger_test (card ^ref-06)
nodes.rationale: Failure-case suite for the generic audit trigger. Coverage sweep: every public table except audit_log carries trg_audit_<table>, and audit_log itself does not (that would recurse). TC-19/TC-20 on lot_receipts: INSERT records actor_id, actor_role, event_date, a null `before`, the weight inside `after`, and the mismatch reason mapped from variance_reason onto the single audit reason column; audit created_at is now() even though the row's own created_at was supplied 26 years stale, and the supplied value survives inside the snapshot; idempotency_key is null on a table that has none. UPDATE keeps both old and new values; DELETE keeps `before` and a null `after`. TC-18: audit_log refuses UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE. Explicitly a failure-mode suite.

nodes.label: branch_daily_schema_test (card ^ref-38)
nodes.rationale: Schema assertions for daily_reports and thaw_records (TC-01 ... TC-09 of TDD-branch-daily-open.md). Written before migration ...0009 and run red on purpose: TC-02, TC-03 and TC-04 failed against the baseline. TC-06 is the inverse assert — a column that must NEVER appear — so the correction cannot drift back in. Also asserts the one-open-day index and fn_open_daily_report's shape.

nodes.label: branch_daily_test (card ^ref-39)
nodes.rationale: Failure-case suite for fn_open_daily_report and fn_require_branch, TC-10 ... TC-32 of TDD-branch-daily-open.md. Asserts: a replay does not re-open a day closed with ready stock at zero (R13); two dates cannot be open at one branch (ADR-014); an L3 with a user_locations row is not let through on membership alone; a deactivated admin does not read as FORBIDDEN; the rice carry-forward reads the most recent rice_records row rather than yesterday; null and 0 are not collapsed; opening a day writes no stock_ledger row and no second audit_log row. TC-33/TC-34 need two sessions and live in branch_daily_concurrency_test.sh. Errors are captured into v_err and asserted after the block so a failing assert inside a `when others` handler cannot report the wrong message.

nodes.label: config_read_test (card ^ref-11 / ^ref-64)
nodes.rationale: Failure-case suite for fn_config_value / fn_config_numeric, TC-01 ... TC-11 of TDD-config-layer.md. Asserts date-effective resolution (a rate entered today must not move a figure settled last month, BR23/ADR-006); an unset key must fail by name rather than resolve to a null a call site coalesces to 0 (BR04, avg_pack_weight_kg); a key/type mismatch must not arrive as a silent null; a global default must not silently override a per-branch value; resolution must not drift to now(). TC-11 (^ref-64) asserts the resolver refuses to answer at all before any JWT claim is set — the revoke on these two functions had turned out to be silently inert, and this is the second mechanism.

nodes.label: config_schema_test (card ^ref-10)
nodes.rationale: Turns ^ref-10's one-time reading into an assertion run on every apply: the six config tables exist; the four rate-bearing ones (smoke_fee_tiers, config_settings, product_prices, packaging_full_stock) carry effective_from, created_by and created_at; no mutable rate column exists anywhere. The last block deliberately asserts that packaging_full_stock's unique key is still BROKEN — (packaging_item_id, location_id, effective_from) with a nullable location_id stores two GLOBAL rows for one date because Postgres treats NULLs as distinct — so the day someone fixes the index the assert fails and points at fn_set_packaging_full_stock's application-code guard as now-dead code.

nodes.label: config_screen_test (card ^ref-12)
nodes.rationale: Failure-case suite for v_config_history, the OW 10 reader, TC-32 ... TC-42 of TDD-config-layer.md. TC-32/TC-33: L2 and L3 sessions read nothing (R20; a hidden menu is not enforcement, ADR-004). TC-34: the Owner still reads, so deny-everyone is not vacuously passing. TC-35: a direct read past the view to the table fails. TC-36: is_current must agree with fn_config_value about what 'current' means. TC-37: is_current is computed per (source, item_key, scope) so a branch override and the global default do not collapse. TC-38: a future-dated row must not render as effective. TC-39: a fee band set is listed as a set, since a gap is a property of the set (D02, R37, fn_set_smoke_fee_tier). TC-40: a retry writes no second row. TC-42: a superseded row stays visible so the append-only rule is not invisible. TC-41 is Manual.

nodes.label: config_writers_test (card ^ref-11)
nodes.rationale: Failure-case suite for the four config setters (fn_set_config, fn_set_product_price, fn_set_smoke_fee_tier, fn_set_packaging_full_stock), TC-11 ... TC-28 and TC-31 of TDD-config-layer.md. Asserts: an L2 or deactivated Owner cannot write a rate (ADR-004, R31); created_by is not a parameter, so a rate change cannot be signed as somebody else; a setter inserts rather than updates, so last month's closed P&L cannot move (BR23); a retry from a dropped connection neither double-writes nor raises into a retry loop (R4); a same-day correction leaves a trace; a band set with a gap, an overlap or no open top band is refused (D02, BR10); a second GLOBAL full-stock row for one date is refused; a zero full-stock level is refused because it becomes a divisor (R9); and the card grants no session SELECT on a price table (ADR-004, R20).

nodes.label: ledger_post_test (card ^ref-14)
nodes.rationale: Failure-case suite for fn_post_ledger, the ledger write primitive: TC-01, TC-02, TC-03, TC-05 ... TC-08 of TDD-ledger-core.md. Asserts that a retry from a dropped Chiang Mai connection neither double-posts nor raises into an infinite retry (ADR-005, R4); a replayed idempotency key with a different payload does not overwrite the original figure; a draw against a tuple with no rows is refused rather than treating SUM-of-nothing as unlimited (BR24); a meat movement without a lot_id is refused (R21, ADR-017); and the function writes no audit row of its own on top of the ^ref-06 trigger (R32). TC-04, two concurrent draws, needs two sessions and lives in ledger_concurrency_test.sh.

nodes.label: ledger_reversal_test (card ^ref-16)
nodes.rationale: Failure-case suite for fn_reverse_ledger_entry, TC-11 ... TC-13 of TDD-ledger-core.md. Asserts the original row is reversed rather than edited or removed, so the trail of what was first believed survives (ADR-003, R1); the reversal links back so the pair is joinable (R2); a row cannot be reversed twice; a REVERSAL row cannot itself be reversed; and a retry of the pair does not double-post because both rows share one derived idempotency key.

nodes.label: ledger_truncate_test (ADR-003 / card ^ref-13)
nodes.rationale: Single failure case: stock_ledger must refuse TRUNCATE. schema_smoke_test.sql already covers UPDATE and DELETE; a `before update or delete` trigger does not fire on TRUNCATE, so the one statement that destroys the entire ledger in a single shot is the one the append-only guard would not see.

nodes.label: ledger_views_test (card ^ref-15)
nodes.rationale: Failure-case suite for v_stock_balance and v_smoke_group_available, TC-09, TC-10 and TC-19 of TDD-ledger-core.md. Asserts balance is SUM(qty_delta) and cannot drift from a stored figure; two lots sharing one smoke date stay separate pickable rows so the FIFO picker can still name the source lot (D01, D05, R21); the picking list is oldest-first so FIFO is not merely advisory; and an L3 session reads zero rows (R20, ADR-004, UAT-15) — enforced by filtering on fn_current_role(), since there is one application database role and L1/L2/L3 is a profiles column. TC-22, the 200 ms measurement at one year of data, stays Manual.

nodes.label: local_harness (Docker test bootstrap)
nodes.rationale: Not part of the schema and never applied to a Supabase project. Creates the smallest surface the migrations actually touch on a bare Postgres container: roles anon, authenticated and service_role; schema auth; auth.users with the columns schema_smoke_test.sql inserts; and public.rls_auto_enable(), the pre-existing project helper migration 0006 revokes execute on but no migration creates. Run against an empty database before the migrations.

nodes.label: opening_balance_test (card ^ref-62)
nodes.rationale: Failure-case suite for fn_record_opening_balance and fn_set_opening_cost, TC-10 ... TC-24, TC-38, TC-39 and TC-41 of TDD-opening-balance.md. This path has no expectation to check itself against — an opening row IS the expectation — so the guards are all there is. Asserts: an opening lot must carry a smoke date or it sorts as newest stock and the oldest meat never leaves (R46); the cut-off must be configured, not defaulted, or the ADR-021 window does not exist (ADR-023, BR23); an Owner cannot count a freezer they are not at; no price reaches the L3 who counted the meat (BR15, R20); a dropped connection cannot post the count twice (R4); and no cost lands on the ledger row (ADR-003, Seam 1).

nodes.label: opening_close_test (card ^ref-62)
nodes.rationale: Failure-case suite for fn_close_opening_balances and fn_backdating_allowed, TC-25 ... TC-37 and TC-40 of TDD-opening-balance.md. Its own file because the close is permanent WITHIN a transaction too, so each case runs inside a plpgsql sub-block and leaves by raising ROLLBACK_TO_OPEN, using the implicit savepoint around a BEGIN ... EXCEPTION block to unwind the close; anything that is not the sentinel is re-raised so an assert still fails the file. Asserts: the close must not succeed over a costless row, which could then never be costed and never re-entered (Seam 1); a retry must not read as a second close of the one operation the Owner cannot undo (R4 against TC-29); an OPENING row must be refused after the close even through fn_post_ledger (Seam 2); R28 must not re-arm by a second mechanism that can disagree with the first (Seam 4); the back-dating boundary must be the same on every screen (R28); unlock_max_days_back must be configured, not assumed as 3 (ADR-023, BR23).

nodes.label: opening_schema_test (card ^ref-62)
nodes.rationale: Schema-shaped failure cases for migrations ...0011 and ...0012, TC-01 and TC-03 ... TC-09 of TDD-opening-balance.md. Asserts OPENING is a movement type so the close switch has something to predicate on; an opening lot cannot carry a phantom PO (the synthetic-round design ADR-021 rejected, reached through the back door); D01's unique FK did not loosen while this card touched its NOT NULL; a cost column keeps its _thb unit suffix; and no cost parameter appears on fn_record_opening_balance, the counter's function, so BR15 stays true. TC-02 — whether migration ...0011 is ALONE in its file — is the one property SQL cannot see and moved to migrations_apply_test.sh.

nodes.label: purchasing_schema_test (card ^ref-18)
nodes.rationale: TC-01 ... TC-04 of TDD-purchasing.md, turning a one-time reading of ...0003_purchasing_production.sql into a standing assertion: suppliers, purchase_orders, po_deliveries and lots exist with the columns the ER names (including the unit-suffixed weight and price columns), and D01's unique FK from lots to po_deliveries holds. A later migration that drops a unit suffix or loosens the unique FK fails the suite instead of passing review.

nodes.label: purchasing_test (card ^ref-19)
nodes.rationale: Failure-case suite for fn_create_po, fn_add_po_delivery and v_po_outstanding, TC-05 ... TC-19 and TC-21 ... TC-33 of TDD-purchasing.md. Asserts: an L2, an L3 or a deactivated Owner cannot raise a PO (ADR-004, R31); created_by and seq are not parameters; a retry books no second round, since every lot, freight share and yield figure downstream would inherit the double (R4); a genuine second identical round is not refused as if it were that retry; a round cannot be booked past the ordered weight; a round is never written without a lot, and the lot's weight is the round's (D01, R16) so BR03's loss base is a weight that actually moved; a lot is dispatched to the chef house, not a branch (BR11); the card posts nothing to stock_ledger, so meat is not in stock days before the truck; and no session SELECT is granted on a price-bearing table (ADR-004, R20). TC-20 needs two sessions and lives in purchasing_concurrency_test.sh.

nodes.label: rls_behaviour_test (card ^ref-64)
nodes.rationale: The behavioural half of the deny-all posture, split out of rls_deny_all_test.sql by ^ref-64: a real `authenticated` session must be refused. Docker-only, because it writes a fixture row to prove the write is refused and supabase/tests/* is never pointed at a real database. Reads locations rather than profiles, since ^ref-05 grants SELECT on profiles behind a self-or-Owner policy so a claimless session there gets zero rows rather than an error. Neither half proves the posture alone — the catalogue can say authenticated holds no grant while a policy hands it rows, and a session can be refused today because a fixture is missing rather than because the grant is.

nodes.label: rls_helpers_test (card ^ref-05)
nodes.rationale: Failure-case suite for fn_current_role, fn_current_locations and the profiles policy. Asserts the helper does not recurse (which would make every policy in the system throw at query time); a deactivated profile loses its role because is_active is checked inside the helper, not somewhere else; fn_current_locations() never returns null, since `= any(null)` quietly matches nothing that anyone verifies; and the grant behind the profiles policy does not open the whole table.

nodes.label: schema_smoke_test (three logic triggers)
nodes.rationale: Smoke test for the three triggers that carry real logic: R6a — smoke_daily_logs.input_weight_kg is the rolled-up sum of its smoke_daily_log_sources rows; R21 — SMOKED_MEAT sales and waste lines must name a lot; R1 — stock_ledger accepts INSERT only (UPDATE and DELETE refused; TRUNCATE is covered separately by ledger_truncate_test.sql). Happy path plus the refusals, in one transaction aborted on purpose.

nodes.label: transport_schema_test (card ^ref-21)
nodes.rationale: TC-01 ... TC-04, TC-21 and TC-38 of TDD-transport.md, asserting the transport_runs / transport_lines schema rather than reading it once: both tables and the columns the ER names, dispatched and received weight kept separately plus variance_reason, the FKs, the unique index and the branch-leg check. TC-38 cross-checks a stored variance column against fn_check_variance so the two cannot disagree, and a grant sweep confirms no session SELECT on the fare-bearing table.

nodes.label: transport_test (cards ^ref-22, ^ref-23)
nodes.rationale: Failure-case suite for fn_create_transport_run, fn_dispatch_transport_line, fn_confirm_transport_receipt, fn_allocate_freight and the three transport views, TC-05 ... TC-37, TC-39 and TC-40 of TDD-transport.md. Asserts: a run cannot be created by an L2, an L3 or a deactivated Owner (ADR-004, R31); the allocation method is frozen on the run rather than chosen by the caller or re-read from config later, so a July config change cannot move a March number (R29, BR23); a return run cannot be created for lots nobody scheduled a pickup for (R26, BR17); a dispatch leaves the in-transit tuple at the right end (Seam 1); a retry posts no second TRANSFER_OUT (Seam 2, R4); a partial receipt is not treated as a full one (D06); a variance past threshold cannot be signed off with no reason (UAT-11, BR12); a branch admin cannot sign for another branch or for the chef house; rounded freight shares sum exactly to the fare (R24, Seam 3); and an L3 session reads no fare (R20, R34). TC-41 needs two sessions and lives in transport_concurrency_test.sh.

nodes.label: variance_test (card ^ref-17)
nodes.rationale: Failure-case suite for fn_check_variance, the one shared variance rule, TC-14 ... TC-18 of TDD-ledger-core.md. Pure arithmetic, no fixtures. Asserts 75 against an expected 100 is 25.00% with verdict OVER_THRESHOLD; a zero expectation takes the explicit branch rather than dividing by zero or quietly reading as '0% off' so an unconfigured figure looks perfect (R22, ADR-019); the boundary does not drift — 20.00 is acceptable and 20.01 is not, and a third decimal does not push 20.004 over; alert-vs-block has no default, so no call site can inherit the wrong one silently (ADR-019); and BLOCK mode aborts rather than returning a verdict the caller can ignore.

Create Next App defaults superseded by project conventions
Transport run: fare snapshot, freight split, and signed receipt
Dated config resolution stack (one lookup, typed readers, never a default)
Audit trail integrity: blanket capture, append-only guard, revoked defaults
Append-only correction: reversal plus replacement
L1-only dated config setters sharing one preamble and BR23
Read views gating role in the WHERE while their tables stay deny-all
Go-live opening balance: a lot with no PO, a cost off the ledger, and a one-way close
Ledger immutability: three triggers closing UPDATE/DELETE, TRUNCATE and post-close OPENING
Traceability chain: supplier batch to dispatch round to lot to smoke-date group to ledger row
FINAL deny-all: the SECURITY DEFINER view is the only read door (no table policy ever lands)
Tables denied outright so an L3 session cannot reach a price or yield column (R20 / BR15)
Provisional deny-all: per-table declaration held until the card owning its role-specific v_* view is written
Tables held deny-all until their role-specific v_* view exists (ADR-002, ADR-004)
The L1 Owner single-read-door pattern: SECURITY DEFINER view gated on fn_current_role(), never a second table policy, and never force RLS
Tables whose closed posture is what keeps price and yield columns away from an L3 session (R20)
Tests that together prove the append-only stock ledger (ADR-003, R1)
Tests that together prove the deny-all RLS posture and the database-side role gate (ADR-004, R20)
Tests asserting the client-generated idempotency key survives a dropped connection (ADR-005, R4)
